title: Multi-stack integration architecture
purpose: External estates connect to governed OneLake through deliberate virtualize, replicate, or copy paths, then serve Fabric and API consumers without hiding security and freshness trade-offs.
accessibleSummary: Multi-stack integration architecture. External data estates; Virtualize with shortcut; Replicate with mirroring; Copy with Data Factory; Governed OneLake hub; Serve BI, APIs and engineering.
longDescription: External estates connect to governed OneLake through deliberate virtualize, replicate, or copy paths, then serve Fabric and API consumers without hiding security and freshness trade-offs.

nodes.label: External data estates
nodes.summary: Operational databases and cloud object stores remain authoritative outside Fabric.
nodes.detail: Source ownership, network reachability, change semantics, and egress constraints frame the integration choice.
nodes.whyItMatters: The architecture begins by respecting systems of record.

drill.example: A Snowflake source and S3 landing zone must feed the same analytics product.
failureModes: Treating every source as a batch-copy candidate.

nodes.label: Virtualize with shortcut
nodes.summary: OneLake shortcuts reference supported external data without creating another physical copy.
nodes.detail: The shortcut presents remote data in the OneLake namespace while the source remains authoritative.
nodes.whyItMatters: Virtualization minimizes duplication when remote access and freshness are acceptable.

evidence.note: OneLake shortcuts expose supported internal and external storage through a virtual reference.
OneLake provides a unified logical namespace for Fabric data.

drill.example: A lakehouse reads governed Parquet in S3 through a shortcut.
failureModes: Remote permissions or egress make reads fail or costly.

nodes.label: Replicate with mirroring
nodes.summary: Mirroring continuously brings supported source changes into Fabric-managed storage.
nodes.detail: A replica supports analytics without redirecting operational ownership to Fabric.
nodes.whyItMatters: Replication is useful when local analytical reads and low-copy-latency matter.

evidence.note: Fabric Mirroring replicates supported operational and analytical sources into OneLake for analytics.

drill.example: A supported database mirrors order changes for near-current BI.
failureModes: Unsupported changes or stalled replication create freshness gaps.

nodes.label: Copy with Data Factory
nodes.summary: Pipelines and Copy activity move bounded snapshots or increments across many connectors.
nodes.detail: Orchestration adds schedules, mappings, branching, retries, and explicit destination ownership.
nodes.whyItMatters: Copy is the flexible path when transformation or controlled materialization is required.

evidence.note: Fabric Data Factory provides pipelines and data movement across sources.
Copy activity supports scalable movement with configurable source and sink behavior.

drill.example: A pipeline copies a nightly Salesforce increment into a bronze lakehouse table.
failureModes: A failed watermark advance skips or duplicates records.

nodes.label: Governed OneLake hub
nodes.summary: Virtual and materialized paths converge in workspaces where ownership, lineage, and security are applied.
nodes.detail: The logical hub lets downstream workloads find data through a consistent Fabric boundary.
nodes.whyItMatters: Convergence is valuable only when access models remain explicit per path.

evidence.note: Fabric governance covers discovery, lineage, labels, access and monitoring.
OneLake security provides data-access controls for governed storage.

drill.example: A domain publishes curated customer data with lineage to both S3 and CRM.
failureModes: A shortcut's source permissions are mistaken for local item ownership.

nodes.label: Serve BI, APIs and engineering
nodes.summary: Fabric workloads consume the governed data through SQL, Spark, semantic models, and GraphQL.
nodes.detail: Serving contracts should match consumer latency, query, and write requirements.
nodes.whyItMatters: A shared hub supports multiple experiences without pretending they use identical engines.

evidence.note: Fabric API for GraphQL provides a typed API over configured Fabric data sources.
A lakehouse SQL analytics endpoint exposes a SQL query surface over lakehouse tables.

drill.example: Power BI reads a semantic model while an app uses GraphQL over a curated source.
failureModes: Consumers assume shortcut, mirror and copy have identical freshness.
